hero.title: Find the solution that matches your problem.
hero.lead: Six ways to work together, from a simple business website to a custom internal tool. If you are unsure, start by describing your business: that question usually settles it.

site-web.name: Business website
site-web.short: Present your business, generate enquiries, build credibility.
site-web.title: A website that represents you, and brings you customers.
site-web.lead: Your website is often the first contact between you and a customer. In a few seconds it decides whether you look serious. We build that first impression.
for: Tradespeople, retailers and independent professionals
Small businesses with no website, or a dated one
Founders launching a new business
Teams fielding enquiries by phone who want to channel them
site-web.problem: You exist, but nobody finds you. Or they find you, and what they see does not reflect the quality of your work. A well-built website fixes both: it makes you visible in your area and it reassures before the first call.
deliver: A 5 to 15 page site, designed around your business
A custom design, not a purchased theme with new colours
A structure built for local search
A contact form that sends you qualified enquiries
features: Map, opening hours and practical details
steps: A conversation to understand your business and your customers
Site structure and content: what each page has to say
Design signed off before any development
Development, with your copy and photos in place
Review together, fixes, then launch
included: Responsive site, tested on phone, tablet and desktop
Domain name and hosting set up
One month of fixes after launch
site-web.after: Your site is alive: new photos, new services, a new page. You can send us those changes one by one or take a monthly maintenance plan. Either way, you own everything.

faq.q: Can I edit the site myself?
faq.a: Yes, if you want to. We can add an admin interface that lets you change text and photos without touching code. If you would rather we handle updates, that works too.

faq.q: Will my site rank well on Google?
faq.a: We ship a technically sound site: fast, structured, properly marked up, readable by Google. That is half the work. The other half is content and time. We show you how to keep it up, without promising you the top spot in three weeks.

faq.q: I already have a domain name, is that a problem?
faq.a: Quite the opposite. We take it over and switch without any downtime.

e-commerce.name: E-commerce
e-commerce.short: Catalogue, payments, orders, customer accounts, admin.
e-commerce.title: An online store you actually run yourself.
e-commerce.lead: Selling online is not just displaying products. It is a checkout that loses nobody, a back office you master, and payments that land.
for: Retailers who want to sell beyond their physical shop
Makers and artisans with a catalogue to move
Brands looking to escape marketplace commissions
Sellers whose current site loses customers at checkout
e-commerce.problem: Most online stores lose customers between the basket and the payment: too many steps, too many fields, not enough reassurance. We build the journey the other way round, starting from what makes people abandon.
deliver: A complete store with catalogue, basket and secure payment
A back office for products, stock and orders
Customer accounts with order history and tracking
Automated emails: confirmation, shipping, basket reminders
features: Shipping, pickup points and delivery costs
steps: Scoping the catalogue, pricing and shipping rules
Designing the checkout, from basket to payment
Designs for the key pages: listing, product, basket
Development, payment and carrier integration
Real test orders before opening
included: Legal pages suited to online selling
One month of fixes after opening
e-commerce.after: A store needs follow-up: payment providers, carriers and legal obligations all change. We handle technical updates and new features as you grow.

faq.a: For a standard catalogue on a tight budget, sometimes yes, and we will say so. Custom takes over as soon as you have unusual business rules, margins to protect, or volume that makes commissions painful.
You do, from the back office. We train you on it, and it is designed to be used daily, not only on launch day.
We use established providers such as Stripe. Card details never pass through your site, and compliance sits with the payment provider.

mobile.name: Mobile app
mobile.short: iOS and Android, authentication, notifications, API, business features.
mobile.title: An app your users keep on their home screen.
mobile.lead: An app is not judged by its number of features, but by how often it gets opened. We build for real use, not for the demo.
for: Businesses that want a direct line to their customers
Services used on the move, in the field
Founders with an idea to validate quickly
Teams that need an internal tool in their pocket
mobile.problem: Many apps are downloaded then forgotten. Usually because they reproduce a website in a smaller frame instead of using what makes mobile unique: notifications, the camera, location, offline use.
deliver: An iOS and Android app from a single codebase
User accounts and authentication
An API and a server-side admin
Publication on the App Store and Play Store
steps: Scoping user journeys and the first release
Designs for the main screens, signed off before development
Development in batches, with a testable build at each step
Testing on real devices, iOS and Android
Store publication and launch support
included: Developer accounts set up in your name
mobile.after: An app lives at the pace of iOS and Android releases. We keep it compatible, fix issues and ship new versions to the stores.

faq.q: Does it have to be built twice, for iOS and Android?
faq.a: No. We use React Native: one codebase produces both apps. That halves the cost and keeps both versions identical over time.

faq.q: How long does store approval take?
faq.a: Apple usually takes a few days, Google is faster. We prepare the listings, screenshots and required notices to avoid rejections.
We recommend it. A tight first version in the hands of real users will teach you more than six months of specifications.

sur-mesure.name: Custom software
sur-mesure.short: Dashboards, client portals, automation, internal tools, APIs.
sur-mesure.title: A tool that fits your business, not the other way round.
sur-mesure.lead: When your company runs on a shared spreadsheet, copy-paste and three systems that do not talk to each other, the problem is no longer your organisation. It is the tool.
for: Companies whose work fits no off-the-shelf software
Teams losing hours to manual data entry
Staff juggling several disconnected tools
Businesses that need a dedicated client portal
sur-mesure.problem: Generic software forces you to bend your business to its constraints. Custom works the other way: the tool takes on your rules, your vocabulary and your steps. What took two hours a day takes ten minutes.
deliver: A web application reachable from any browser
A dashboard with the numbers that actually matter
Roles and permissions per user
Connections to the tools you already use
features: Client portal with documents and tracking
API connections to your current software
steps: Immersion: understanding how you actually work today
Mapping processes and spotting where time is lost
Scoping a first release around what pays off fastest
Development in batches with progressive rollout
Team training and change support
sur-mesure.after: A business tool evolves with the company. We stay available for adjustments, new needs and onboarding new users.

faq.q: What if my needs change mid-project?
faq.a: That is the norm, not the exception: you understand your needs better once you see the tool take shape. We work in batches to absorb that, and any change of scope is quoted before it is committed.

faq.q: Can you connect our existing software?
faq.a: In most cases yes, provided it offers an API or exports. We check this during scoping, before any commitment.

faq.q: What happens if we stop working together?
faq.a: You leave with everything: source code, database, server access and documentation. We keep no key that would make you dependent.

refonte.name: Redesign & optimisation
refonte.short: Modernisation, responsive, UX, performance, technical SEO.
refonte.title: Your site already exists. Let's make it work.
refonte.lead: Rebuilding everything is not always the right answer. Sometimes a slow site, broken on mobile or unreadable to Google, can be rescued without starting over.
for: Sites over five years old that show their age
Slow sites, poorly rated or broken on mobile
Businesses whose brand has moved on but whose site has not
Owners who have lost control of their current site
refonte.problem: A dated site does not just look old: it is slower, ranks worse and inspires less trust. A redesign fixes all three together, while keeping what already works.
deliver: An audit of what exists: performance, mobile, SEO, security
A recommendation on what to rebuild and what to keep
A redesign of the look and the experience
Migration without losing search rankings
steps: Full audit and debrief: what works, what does not, what it costs
Deciding between optimisation and a full rebuild
Designing the new pages
Development and content migration
Switchover with redirects and search monitoring
included: One month of monitoring after the switch
refonte.after: We watch rankings and performance in the weeks after the switch, when problems surface. Then maintenance takes over.

faq.q: Will I lose my search rankings?
faq.a: That is the main risk of a redesign, and it is manageable: a redirect plan, keeping the URLs that work, preserving structure, monitoring afterwards. Done properly, a redesign improves rankings.

faq.q: Can you take over a site built by someone else?
faq.a: Yes, it happens often. We start with an audit to see what is salvageable. Sometimes starting fresh costs less than repairing, and we will tell you straight.

faq.q: What if I have lost access to my site?
faq.a: We help you recover it from the host or registrar. It is usually possible, even without the original supplier.

maintenance.name: Maintenance & support
maintenance.short: Fixes, security, updates and new features.
maintenance.title: A site that has shipped is not a site that is finished.
maintenance.lead: Browsers change, dependencies age, vulnerabilities appear. Without upkeep, a perfectly working site becomes a liability within eighteen months.
for: Clients whose site or app we built
Businesses whose supplier has vanished or stopped replying
Teams with nobody in-house on the technical side
Sites the business depends on, that cannot go down
maintenance.problem: Without maintenance, the question is not whether something will break, but when. And it always breaks at the worst moment: a Friday evening, mid-season.
deliver: Technical and security updates
Uptime and performance monitoring
Regular, tested backups
Someone reachable when things break
steps: Technical review of the site or app
Setting up monitoring and backups
Agreeing service levels and response times
Monthly follow-up with a readable report
Changes planned together
included: An allowance of hours for changes, depending on the plan
maintenance.after: Maintenance is a monthly commitment with no minimum term. You can stop whenever you like and you leave with every access you need.

faq.a: Never. It is optional, and we will tell you honestly whether your site really needs it or can go without for a while.

faq.q: What happens when there is a bug?
faq.a: You write to us, we diagnose, we fix. Response times are written into the contract, not left to the mood of the day.

faq.q: Can you maintain a site you did not build?
faq.a: Yes, after an audit. We first need to check the code is in a state where we can work safely.
